clinician.trajectory_summary: A 35-year-old male smoker with no significant past medical history presented on day 0 with sudden-onset expressive and receptive dysphasia, mild confusion, and right arm incoordination (NIH Stroke Scale 5). Initial CT brain was normal. He was treated with thrombolysis for suspected ischaemic stroke, and initial symptoms resolved over 2 hours. However, on day 3, he developed recurrent right arm weakness, expressive and receptive dysphasia, amnesia, headache, vomiting, and pyrexia (39.7°C). Brain MRI on day 3 was normal. Lumbar puncture on day 4 revealed lymphocytic pleocytosis (WBC 134 × 10^6/L, 99% lymphocytes), normal protein (0.52 g/L), and normal CSF:serum glucose ratio (0.73), consistent with viral meningitis/encephalitis. CSF SARS-CoV-2 PCR was positive with identification of both E gene (CT 35.8) and S gene (CT 35.7) using the Altona RealStar SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR Kit on the Roche Flow system, confirming SARS-CoV-2 encephalitis. Nasopharyngeal swab was negative for SARS-CoV-2, and the patient had no respiratory symptoms, indicating CNS-predominant viral infection. Pyrexia and amnesia persisted until day 8, when the patient was deemed to have made a full recovery and was discharged.
